lf_clicks_leakage.A3_clicks_K1: Unchanged verdict. Earthing adds the fan-frame capacitance (50-300 pF) as a CM path for the contact-arc transients, so click amplitudes can rise; the verdict rests on 5.4.3.2 / 5.4.3.4 (EN 55014-1 PDF p. 50-51), which do not depend on amplitude (N 0.017/min, clicks <= 3.3 ms). Not re-run.
lf_clicks_leakage.A3_clicks_triac: Changes only through A1: without a fix the earthed CM level exceeds the IF reference level, so each firing burst is a 'disturbance other than clicks' (4.4.2.2) and the continuous limit applies - i.e. the A1 FAIL. With the fix + F1 the envelope is below the limit (A1 margin >= 8.7 dB), no clicks registered.
lf_clicks_leakage.A4_harmonics: Unchanged: 50 Hz-2 kHz currents are set by the heater, HLK and fan; the chassis earth carries only capacitive leakage (< 0.1 mA). The proposed 200 uH A1-lead inductor shifts the heater current by 0.068 deg at 50 Hz and lengthens the turn-on rise (L/R = 3.8 us) - negligible against the 20.5 % worst harmonic. Not re-run.
lf_clicks_leakage.A5_flicker: Unchanged: earthing does not change the L-N current steps. The fix adds 2 x 0.1 ohm in series (dU change 0.378 % of U) - negligible. Not re-run.
lf_clicks_leakage.fix_power_note: 2 x RC1415U-101K (0.10 ohm each, spec 12.5 / BOM) at 4.35 A rms -> ~1.9 W each, the same as L40; place them away from HS1 and C40

leakage_current.limit: class I portable appliance 0.75 mA - IEC 60335-1 clause 13/16 NOT READ FROM THE STANDARD; public source: Bel Fuse / CUI blog 'IEC 60335-1 explained' (0.75 mA portable, 3.5 mA stationary)
leakage_current.Y_cap_budget_note: Y capacitors are NOT part of the chosen fix. Had they been used: 2.2 nF L-PE at 1.06 x 230 V -> 0.17 mA, 4.7 nF -> 0.36 mA (budget 0.75 mA minus heater insulation leakage)
